Storyline Newark. Twenty players participated, and I won it. Mark's
synopsis will be posted when it is complete. Here is my winning deck:

I stole the chump Justicar idea from Matt Heslin, who stole it from Ben
Peal. I had a goal of screwing with the World of Darkness in this Storyline
format. I understand that the Gangrel have left the Camarilla in the clan
novels. I like that my weenie Gangrel not only were Camarilla, but they
elected a Justicar and then did wacky Justicar stuff. Thanks to Mr. Heslin
for deck pointers and to Mr. Loughman for holding the event (and for
allowing me to use Archon Investigation on his Lazverinus, Thrall of Lambach
in the final).

Can I wear this Jacket?
Jay

Messages.Author: Jay Kristoff
Messages.Body:
Bernie wrote:
>That's one of the most Bizarre decks I've seen posted in some time,
>would you elaborate a bit on how the deck flows?

For you Bernie, anything! The name of the deck "Can I wear this
jacket?" comes from the art on the Gangrel Justicar card. That funky brown
leather fringe jacket is probably the bomb in Southern Ohio and other
Gangrel type places. When I called that G.J. vote I would ask the other
players "can I wear this jacket?". Many times I didn't need their approval
to wear it. The special text on the Justicar vote "In this <referendum>,
each Gangrel gets 1 extra vote" meant that I could usually pass it.
Sometimes I would get my first G.J. passed on turn two (I had two votes for
it passing), or other times I had to wait until later in the game when I had
a swarm of green vamps to help pass the vote.
After I successfully pass my first G.J. the ball starts rolling. The
"trick" of the deck comes from rule section 6.3.4 "a vampire cannot have
more than one title. If a vampire with a title gains another, he loses the
first title, even if the new title would be a demotion". So... later in the
game I call another G.J. I name my Gangrel that already has the Justicar
title. The vote passes tremendously (I have 12 or so votes in favor). The
Justicar yields his old title and puts on the new jacket. Then I play
cryptic rider. The rider vote was usually a Consag. Boon (Gangrel); or any
of the other cool votes in the deck (Justicar Retribution, Dramatic
Upheaval, etc.). The C. Boons were paying off well with my army of Gangrel.
Other special tricks in the deck include:
-up to four master phase actions in a turn
-play ToGP on a vamp more than once in one master phase
-buy your prey's one big vamp with ToGP and then call Ancient Influence
-Info Highway + Eco Terrorist = many green dudes
-with Sanguine Instruction my chumps became masterful at Protean
-Elder Library +Semsith = no pain, all gain
The deck was fun to play, but it was difficult to keep track of all the
permanents I had in front of me. Toward the end of the final round people
were physically helping me untap everything because it took so long.
Bernie, you'll see other strange Buckeyes, and myself on May 4th!
take care,
Jay Kristoff, V:EKN Prince of Columbus Ohio
